proposals.title: Graph-Based Adaptive Spatial Domain Segmentation
proposals.summary: This analysis employs graph-based clustering that integrates gene expression similarity with the spatial coordinates of each capture spot. By constructing a weighted spatial graph, the method identifies biologically meaningful regions while accounting for gradual transitions and sharp boundaries in tissue sections. The approach leverages neighborhood connectivity to optimize clustering and can be tuned to avoid fragmentation of domains, providing robust segmentation even in sparse data settings.

proposals.title: Edge-Aware Expression Smoothing for Boundary Preservation
proposals.summary: This approach applies advanced edge-aware smoothing methods to the spatial transcriptomics data to reduce noise without blurring genuine biological boundaries. By incorporating techniques such as bilateral filtering and adaptive kernel smoothing, the analysis detects and respects abrupt changes in gene expression at region interfaces, ensuring that the smoothed patterns remain true to underlying tissue architecture. This method is particularly useful in resolving local expression variations while maintaining critical domain edges.

proposals.title: 3D Tissue Reconstruction from Consecutive Spatial Sections
proposals.summary: In this analysis, spatial transcriptomics data collected from serial tissue sections are aligned and integrated to reconstruct a three-dimensional tissue architecture. The method involves correcting for section-specific effects, aligning spatial landmarks across sections, and combining local gene expression profiles to create a coherent 3D representation. This approach enables a deeper understanding of tissue organization and facilitates the discovery of spatial patterns that span multiple sections.

proposals.title: Dimensionality Reduction Incorporating Spatial Context
proposals.summary: This analysis develops a low-dimensional embedding technique that integrates traditional gene expression profiles with spatial neighborhood information. By using manifold learning or adapted PCA methods that weigh spatial relationships, the method produces embeddings that preserve both local and global tissue architectures. This representation enhances the detection of subtle biological gradients and mixed cell-type regions, supporting downstream clustering and interpretation of spatial heterogeneity.

proposals.title: Cross-Sectional Batch Correction with Spatial Metrics
proposals.summary: Here, the focus is on developing a batch correction framework tailored for spatial transcriptomics data collected from different sections. By leveraging spatial distribution metrics and incorporating local neighborhood information, the method adjusts for section-specific artifacts while preserving the intrinsic spatial relationships within the data. This analysis not only normalizes across experiments but also ensures that biological domain boundaries remain distinct.

proposals.title: Nonlinear Smoothing with Boundary-Conscious Regularization
proposals.summary: This analysis explores nonlinear smoothing techniques that incorporate regularization penalties specifically designed to maintain sharp boundaries between distinct tissue domains. Utilizing algorithms such as total variation minimization adapted for spatial data, the method smooths noise in gene expression measurements while limiting spillover effects across domain edges. This strategy results in clearer demarcation of regions and more accurate representation of cellular distributions.

proposals.title: Spatial Graph-Based Neighborhood Analysis for Domain Recovery
proposals.summary: Focusing on the construction of a spatial neighborhood graph, this analysis uses connectivity and distance metrics to identify and validate coherent biological domains from spatial transcriptomics data. Graph community detection algorithms are applied to identify clusters that reflect true tissue compartments, even in the presence of gradual transitions. This method helps to elucidate subtle spatial relationships and recover biologically relevant domain structures.

proposals.title: Integrative Multi-Omics Spatial Analysis
proposals.summary: This analysis integrates spatial transcriptomics with complementary spatial omics data (e.g., spatial proteomics or metabolomics) to enhance the resolution of tissue domain characterization. Using joint dimensionality reduction techniques and cross-modal batch correction, the approach identifies multi-layered spatial patterns. This integrative strategy not only improves noise reduction and domain delineation but also provides a more comprehensive view of tissue microenvironments.

proposals.title: Noise Reduction via Spatial Filtering with Precision Boundary Control
proposals.summary: This analysis employs spatial filtering techniques, such as diffusion or wavelet transforms, tailored to the characteristics of spatial transcriptomics data. The focus is on reducing technical and measurement noise while precisely preserving expression discontinuities at boundaries. The method carefully calibrates filter parameters based on local spatial density and expression variance, ensuring that the resulting expression maps faithfully represent underlying biological domain structures.
